html:
British Tripolitania was north west Libya under British military rule, from the fall of Tripoli in January 1943 until Libya became independent in 1951.

Tripolitania held most of Libya's people and its capital, Tripoli. Many Italian settlers stayed on under the British. The great powers argued over its future. In 1949 a British and Italian plan, the Bevin and Sforza plan, proposed to hand Tripolitania back to Italy as a trust territory. Crowds in Tripoli protested, and the plan failed by a single vote at the United Nations.

The United Nations then voted that all of Libya should be independent. Tripolitania joined Cyrenaica and the Fezzan in the Kingdom of Libya in 1951, the first African country to win independence through the United Nations.
sum: British Tripolitania was north west Libya under British military rule, from the fall of Tripoli in January 1943 until Libya became independent in 1951.
